title: Does Gravity Care Which Path? Explained Simply | Class 11 Physics
description:
Carry a bag up the stairs or up a long ramp. Ride up a steep road or a winding one. You end at the same height, so does gravity care which way you went? Aarav can reach the hilltop by a steep 300 m path or a 1.2 km winding road, both climbing 60 m. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Physics (Chapter 5, Work, Energy and Power) for NCERT, CBSE, ISC and PUC students, plus JEE Main and NEET, we learn conservative and non-conservative forces.

On a live simulation a 3 kg box goes from the floor to a shelf 2 m up by three paths: straight up then across, up a 30 degree ramp, and up a staircase. The graph of work by gravity against path length shows three different lengths ending at the same -58.8 J, and the round trip comes back to zero. A slow-mo replay shows why: only the up and down part of the motion counts. We prove W = -mg(y2 - y1) step by step, follow friction link by link to see why its round trip work is never zero, compare a short and a long slide, and work out gravity and resistance on Aarav's two paths. Then the exam trap about zero work, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

In this video:
0:00 Two ways up, same height
0:30 What is a conservative force?
0:54 Live simulation: three paths to one shelf
1:36 Why only height counts, step by step
2:21 Friction, link by link
2:43 Short way vs long way + pause and think
3:33 Worked example: the steep path and the winding road
4:12 Exam trap: is the work always zero?
4:32 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:25 Recap and three questions to answer
